question: where the presence skip rate drops after the noqa fragment rewrite (89.16% -> 87.76% skipped (file, rule) pairs on full Django), and what L-span (conditions L1-L3) changes
measured: fragment-rewrite design 4.1: the presence diagnostic (presence_file events) of a full Django run, 2,875 files x 413 rules, on the step-2 worker with the rewrite's assets; step 2 alone 1,058,711 of 1,187,375 skipped (89.16%), with the rewrite 1,042,023 (87.76%)

where.files: the 58 of 2,875 Django files with a comment matching (?i:noqa) (164 comments); on them 114 of 23,954 pairs skip (0.48%); on the other 2,817 files the rate is unchanged (89.56%)
where.cause: the shared grammar every suppressing rule calls holds six source-matches steps (noqa-heads 2, noqa-codes 2, noqa-blankets 2). operator/contract/service.rs::failure declares every SourceMatches RowFailure::OnRows(input 0), so the presence fold ORs the presence of their input (comment rows matching (?i:noqa)) into the skip formula of every node downstream: on a file with a noqa comment every suppressing rule is admitted, with or without a candidate
where.already_removed: RUF100's span-between (OnRows) is in RUF100 itself, which is pinned (rewrite part 1); noqa-ranges keeps ordered-match (OnRows 0,1) over range directives, as before the rewrite; Django has none

hypotheses.hypothesis: the give-back is confined to files with a noqa comment and comes from the failure terms of the shared grammar's source-matches steps, not from the rewrite's presence formulas
hypotheses.evidence: design 4.1 presence runs on Django: the 2,817 files without a noqa comment skip 89.56%, as with step 2 alone; the 58 noqa files skip 0.48%; the measurement-only variant with no fallible step in the shared grammar (the old capture grammar) skips 1,059,455 pairs (89.23%), every rule's skipped-file count equal to step 2's except I001 (+744)

hypotheses.hypothesis: origin lineage is enough to call the searched spans located
hypotheses.evidence: noqa-heads ends in union(inline_shaped, file_shaped) and noqa-codes searches heads.suffix_span; the fold resets origins at a Union (operation_schema/projection.rs::output_origins answers no origin for a Union), so noqa-codes and noqa-blankets would stay fallible (review 2, L2)

why_the_fold_keeps_them: InvalidSourceMatchSpan when the input span is out of order, outside the file's bytes or off a UTF-8 boundary (operator/contract/views.rs::source_slice), or base_line <= 0
ShapeMismatch when the span cell is not a Span
InvalidRegex when the literal pattern does not compile (prepared slot, first use) or its named capture is missing (operator/contract/driver.rs::missing_capture)
WrongOperation from contract.row_error (an appended capture output without a capture, an appended line without base_line)
expected: the measurement-only plan shape with no fallible step in the shared grammar skipped 1,059,455 pairs (89.23%), every rule as in step 2 plus 744 I001 skips, output byte-identical (design 4.1); gate: skipped pairs >= 1,058,711 (89.16%)

levers.change: SourceMatches declares no failure only when the step is PerFile, its span column is a Span column, base_line is None, row_error is None, and, in the fold, its literal pattern compiled eagerly into the request's prepared-matcher slot with its named capture present; every other SourceMatches keeps OnRows(input 0)

located is its own per-column flag in the presence fold, mapped by output_origins: set at a Span column of a current-file provider relation and at the match and capture spans of a SourceMatches over a located span, kept through Select, Project, Extend, Join and Antijoin, ANDed across both sides of a Union, absent everywhere else; the origin lattice, which resets at a Union, is unchanged

the provider span columns a never-failing SourceMatches relies on are listed in the presence table and validated at fact admission (the file's first presence read of the relation) with the operator's own span check; a violation turns the file's presence gate off, so every rule runs in full and meets the error as it would have
